newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end sharply lower.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures fell by their 500 yen per tonne daily limits early on and retained those losses by the end of trade on Thursday, depressed by sharp losses in the Chicago market overnight, traders said.
The most-active benchmark March contract plunged by its limit of 500 yen to end at 15,710 yen. Daily volume was estimated at 47,960 lots.

"Active selling by private investors emerged from the outset, due to losses in Chicago overnight," an analyst at a commodity broker said. "Corn futures are likely to fall further amid bearish sentiment," he said.

Traders said all corn and soybean futures on the CBOT Project A trading system were also lower during Asian hours as market players sold contracts in anticipation of further losses in the Chicago market on Thursday.
The spot March contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.96-1/4 per bushel at 0817 GMT, compared with Wednesday's close of $2.97-3/4.
The CBOT soybean futures spot March contract was at $8.17-1/4 at 0817 GMT, down from $8.22-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
